newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open steady, OTC stocks ease.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open steady, OTC stocks ease.

text.p: Singapore shares were mostly steady at the open on Wednesday with profit-taking seen in Malaysian over-the-counter stocks (OTC) after recent gains.

"We saw a wave of profit-taking yesterday afternoon and it is continuing this morning. It is quite healthy for the market to take some profit first - it was looking overbought," said a broker with a local firm.

Dealers said the market's undertone remained firm despite the uncertainty on Wall Street. The UOB-OTC index was down 3.57 points to 1,284.90 while the key Straits Times Industrial index was up 0.08 points to 2,226.38 at 0224 GMT.
Total market volume was an active 116.8 million shares with 114 gainers nudging 103 losers.

Topping the actives list was newly listed Jade Technologies with 26 million shares traded. It was near Singapore $1.02 (US$0.73) against its initial offer price of S$0.75."Fair value is around S$0.95. But it is above because the issue is small," said a dealer.
Shares of Scotts Holdings rose eight cents to S$1.30 on news that an ex-managing director had bought a stake in the company.
Gainers include Creative Technologies, OCBC foreign and SPH foreign, up between S$0.30 and S0.60 each.
